findings: Unspecified-policy legacy winner0 remains available after context exit and through real v1 save/load.
Explicit graph-policy winner1 is reachable inside its memory-only scope; plain v1 saving omits it and bare lookup returns legacy0 or fallback on a graph-only process.
Replay can accept wrong-policy legacy file0. Graph tuning rejects mismatched provenance and profiles1; replay must not be confused with a nested outer active tuning context.
Loading phase files into the same singleton is last-wins for overlapping keys; separate filenames alone do not isolate identities.
Guarded detached export and isolated file-bank activation preserve winner1 after fresh-process reload with zero profiling while bare legacy lookup keeps0.
Wrong-policy, modified cache bytes, existing export paths and shadowing live graph memory are rejected; normal/exceptional activation preserves recorded live banks and original file-map identities.
V1 per-entry provenance omits full timer identity, and a unique fresh output filename does not force an existing memory winner to retune.
